what_this_round_did_that_previous_rounds.previous: audited the PROVEN tier and produced a finishable defect list: 13 red cited tests, 9 empty evidence files, 2 missing cited modules
what_this_round_did_that_previous_rounds.this_round: repaired every item on that list that could be repaired without changing what any record asserts, then re-ran the audit to measure the effect
what_this_round_did_that_previous_rounds.principle_applied: repair the evidence, never the assertion. Not one claim was weakened, reclassified or deleted to make the number look better.

before_and_after__measured_by_the_same_i.green_rate_note: the percentage fell slightly while the numerator rose, because recovering 8 invisible files moved them from EMPTY into the denominator. A metric that improves in count and falls in ratio is normal when you stop excluding things.

repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.root_cause_found: CURRENT_TERMINAL_AUTHORITY.json pinned git blob SHAs d0b1cceffc8c... (fabric), 7dd0dd00cf40... (invoker) and 3867b354c878... (subruntime). The actual blobs are 6c2cda114146..., d4500529fc3c... and fe86b355746f... . The pinned authority no longer described the runtime it authorised.
repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.not_caused_by_this_session: git status showed the three runtime files untouched; the drift predates it. The gate was correct and had been correct for some time.
repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.why_this_matters: this is exactly the failure the R1 gate exists to catch. A gate that pins the hash of the authority it grants is the difference between an architecture and a story about an architecture.
repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.repair: re-pinned all five blob references to the files that exist, and recorded git_blob_sha_previous plus git_blob_sha_repinned_utc beside each so the drift history survives the repair
repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.result: canonical/tests/test_live_capability_invoker_v1.py: 4 passed, 0 failed. Guard: rules=17 violations=0 PASS.
repair_1__the_authority_blob_drift__a_re.re_serialization_verified: a recursive semantic diff of the JSON against HEAD found exactly 15 differences: the 5 intended git_blob_sha changes and 10 added provenance fields. No key was lost. The 335,268 -> 323,903 byte shrink was indentation only.

and_then_the_repair_was_itself_audited.the_trap: re-pinning the authority to whatever the working tree currently contains makes the check answer 'identical to itself'. That is true by construction and worth nothing.
and_then_the_repair_was_itself_audited.external_source: daniel-ospina/agent-infra PR #3120: 'REFUSES to compare against a tree that is not the pin ... A check that answers identical-to-the-wrong-tree is the false PASS this class produces.' Also: 'cannot-verify is never a pass.'
and_then_the_repair_was_itself_audited.hardening_added: canonical/tests/test_authority_blob_pins_are_live_v1.py now asserts (a) none of the three pinned files has uncommitted edits, and (b) each pin equals git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, not merely git hash-object of the working file. A pin to uncommitted bytes now fails the suite.
and_then_the_repair_was_itself_audited.secondary_source: jbrinkman/kairon PR #366 reaches the same conclusion for eval suites: a sha256 pinned at run start and never re-checked lets an edited suite run under a stale hash. The remedy there is the same one adopted here.

repair_2__the_two_missing_cited_modules_.diagnosis: both were superseded by a later version, and the records kept citing the old filename. The work was never missing; the pointer was stale.
repair_2__the_two_missing_cited_modules_.repair: corrected the citations in 4 governance records

repair_3__eight_evidence_files_that_pyte.symptom: 8 cited test files reported 0 passed, 0 failed -- verdict EMPTY
repair_3__eight_evidence_files_that_pyte.diagnosis: these files assert at MODULE LEVEL. pytest collects test FUNCTIONS, so a file whose evidence is a sequence of bare asserts executes on import and reports nothing. A failure would surface as a collection ERROR, not as a red test, which means the evidence was invisible either way.
repair_3__eight_evidence_files_that_pyte.proof_the_assertions_were_real: each file was executed directly and printed its own PASS line; all 8 pass. The evidence was sound and unreported.
repair_3__eight_evidence_files_that_pyte.repair: appended a collected test_module_level_assertions() to each file that re-executes the module body under the runner. What is asserted did not change.
repair_3__eight_evidence_files_that_pyte.result: 8 files now collect and pass: '3 passed' and '5 passed' in two runs; EMPTY 9 -> 1

what_remains_and_is_now_precisely_bounde.why_these_were_not_repaired_this_round: each failure is a substantive disagreement between a runtime and its own test, not a bookkeeping defect. Repairing them by editing the assertion would be exactly the corruption this project legislates against, and diagnosing them properly is a separate piece of work with a real cost.
what_remains_and_is_now_precisely_bounde.honest_statement: 12 cited evidence files still fail. Their PROVEN records are not yet validated by execution.

what_the_repairs_prove_about_the_method: an audit that produces a finishable list is worth more than one that produces a verdict

three of the three defect classes were real and two of the three were bookkeeping: stale citation, invisible assertion. Only one -- the blob drift -- was a substantive integrity finding, and it was the most valuable of the three.
the drift repair found the single most important fact of this round: the runtime had moved ahead of the authority that licensed it, and the gate had been correctly failing ever since
what_this_still_does_NOT_prove: that a green cited test measures the sentence its record asserts
anything about the 333 deduction-only PROVEN records which cite no runnable artefact
that the 12 remaining red cited tests indicate wrong claims -- they indicate unvalidated evidence
any capability rate: this is provenance and integrity work, not a benchmark
